title: Overload, queues, and retry amplification
description: Walk a latency collapse into admission control. Queues convert load to delay. Unbounded retries are the second outage.
assumptions: Primary and app have finite concurrency. Excess wait is a queue, even if you did not name it.
429 with Retry-After is a proven signal. Timeout is UNKNOWN.
TokenX fail closed under overload; ads may sample.

steps.title: Healthy concurrency
steps.timeline: t0: utilization 60–70%. Queue wait small vs service time.
steps.recovery: Watch utilization, queue depth, and timeout rate separately.

steps.title: Detect overload
steps.timeline: t1: arrival rate exceeds service rate. Queue depth grows. p99 crosses SLO.
steps.consistency: Overload does not change isolation level — it changes completion.
steps.durability: In-flight commits still on the primary path if they get a connection.
steps.recovery: Do not only add replicas without admission — that can amplify writes.

steps.title: In-flight timeout
steps.timeline: t1–t2: callers hit timeout while work continues on the server.
steps.inFlight: Server may still commit. Client sees UNKNOWN.
steps.userVisible: Errors plus duplicate side effects if retried blindly.
steps.recovery: Cancel where you can; still treat as UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Admission, not promotion
steps.timeline: t2: shed load. 429 or drop. Do not promote a replica to ‘absorb writes.’
steps.inFlight: Rejected requests never reached the uniqueness store.
steps.consistency: Shed reads may be OK if derived. Shed TokenX writes is fail closed — correct.

steps.title: Retry amplification
steps.timeline: t2–t3: clients retry immediately. Effective arrival rate multiplies.
steps.inFlight: Each logical user action becomes N server attempts.
steps.recovery: Honor Retry-After, jitter, cap attempts, hedging only for safe reads.

steps.title: Degradation policy
steps.inFlight: Read-only mode, cached catalogs, drop ads windows, keep ledger closed.
steps.consistency: Stale catalog is allowed only if named. Stale balances are not TokenX settlement.
steps.userVisible: Partial product: browse yes, pay no — if that is the policy.

steps.title: Drain queues
steps.timeline: t4: arrival drops or capacity rises. Drain depth / extra-capacity with units.
steps.inFlight: Oldest waiters complete or time out.
steps.durability: No catch-up magic for timed-out UNKNOWN writes except keyed retry.
steps.userVisible: Latency returns from the front of the queue first if unfair; name scheduling.
steps.recovery: Autoscale is slow relative to retry storms — admission first.

steps.title: User-visible outcome
steps.timeline: End: SLO burn, some 429, some UNKNOWN, no silent double charge if keys existed.
steps.consistency: Policy held or you have an incident.
steps.durability: Primary intact unless you also hit disk/CPU death.
steps.recovery: Load test the retry policy, not only the happy QPS.
